_comment: EXT-63 — the EXTERNAL-CONSTRAINT arm of the golden-63 lineage.  Same 61 in-network GPS
stations and the same WTZZ00DEU colocated consumer holdout as _golden63_gps_1h_laneoff,
with the satellite parameter block progressively handed to the precise COD products:
ORBIT        external (COD SP3) — already true in every arm
CODE BIAS    external (COD .BIA OSB)      <- network.external_sat_code_bias  (rung C)
PHASE BIAS   external (COD .BIA OSB) PLUS a still-estimated residual state
CLOCK        soft-HELD at the precise .CLK <- clock_datum_broadcast_anchored (rung B)
IONOSPHERE   still co-estimated (SH-VTEC deg 8)
PURPOSE: isolate where the network fails by removing, one family at a time, the
satellite parameters it would otherwise have to determine itself.  If the receiver side
(rx clock, rx DCB, ZWD, slant iono, ambiguities) and the held-out consumer are stable
under external satellite products, the front end and the per-station model are sound and
the defect is in the shared-parameter / datum layer.  If they are NOT stable, the defect
is upstream of the datum entirely and no amount of S-basis work will fix it.
WHY THE BORDER IS STILL NON-EMPTY (this is deliberate).  Fixing EVERY satellite
parameter with a free slant iono would empty the shared border and block-diagonalize the
arrowhead into 61 independent single-station PPP solves — every mechanism under
suspicion (datum realization, rank gate, pivot/handover, carry, SBC/PA) would be
BYPASSED, not validated.  Two things keep it a network: the SH-VTEC field (a shared
block that couples every station and contains no satellite hardware parameter), and the
still-estimated satellite PHASE BIAS (whose gauge is the Card-4 eq34 chain datum).  The
clock hold is SOFT for the same reason — sigma is a continuous dial from fully-external
to fully-self-contained through one code path, not an on/off switch.
WHY DUAL FREQUENCY — this is a THEORY result, not a compromise.
1. COD0MGXFIN_20241290000_01D_01D_OSB.BIA carries GPS C1C/C1L/C1W/C1X, C2L/C2S/C2W/C2X
and L1C/L1L/L1W/L1X, L2L/L2S/L2W/L2X for all 32 satellites and ZERO C5/L5 entries.
Under frequency_mode:triple the third band's satellite delay would be uncorrected at
FULL weight (no_bia_code_downweight is 1.0 on this lineage) with no state to absorb
it, and under an SH constraint it leaks straight into the iono field.
2. The .BIA header declares SATELLITE_CLOCK_REFERENCE_OBSERVABLES G C1W C2W — consuming
COD's clock means adopting COD's IF(C1W,C2W) basis, which is dual by construction.
3. Odijk et al. 2016: the code biases on the first two frequencies are absorbed by the
clock (IF part) and the ionosphere (GF part), so there IS no estimable satellite OSB
under dual — which is exactly why 'dual + estimate_sat_code_bias' gives ZERO solved
epochs (_golden63_gps_1h_dual.json).  Taking the biases from the product instead is
the CONFORMANT dual model, and the product supplies precisely that absorbed split.
CONSISTENCY GATES (user-directed).  With every satellite parameter pinned, nothing is
left to absorb a modelling mismatch — it lands in the iono state and the ambiguities,
the exact quantities being validated.  So both coverage gates are armed:
- model_corrections.require_atx_coverage: strict per-signal ATX coverage (finite PCO +
populated PCV, satellite AND receiver, no fallback chain).  Near-inert on GPS L1/L2
with igs20.atx; exclude_unmodeled_antenna_stations already handles the station case.
- estimation.require_bia_for_signals: a CODE signal with no .BIA entry is dropped
rather than run uncorrected.  Live here (estimate_sat_biases off, .BIA applying).
NOTE it gates CODE only — a phase signal with no phase OSB survives and the float
ambiguity absorbs its bias.  Moot on L1/L2, where COD covers both.
ANCHOR SIGMA.  0.02 m = the .CLK's own precision scale.  Realized clock common-mode
eigenvalue is 1/sigma^2 = 2500, far above the rank-gate cutoff (~1e-9*smax), and the
anchors ARE the datum (declared_dimension 0, no pivot, no handover seam) — so the
clock<->phase-bias trade that produces the ~80 m split drift is structurally closed.
WHAT NOT TO GRADE.  The emitted satellite clock is the precise product plus a
sigma-bounded residual BY CONSTRUCTION; grading it against the .CLK measures the anchor,
not the network.  Grade: (a) the satellite-clock RESIDUAL state in BETWEEN-SATELLITE
form (it should sit near zero and flat — a per-satellite offset that does NOT is a
convention mismatch between our model and COD's, which is the whole point of the arm);
(b) SH a00 against the 30-33 TECU field truth; (c) the held-out WTZZ00DEU consumer
position; (d) the run-end counters (withholds, PA heals, SBC fires, RAIM).
KNOWN-INERT under this posture (expected in the log, invariant #4 — named, not hidden):
- network.code_datum_time_linked warns INERT (no W6 code-bias datum to re-time).  It is
KEPT ON deliberately: turning it off FORCES carry_rx_code_bias off (:6471), and the
rx code-bias carry IS meaningful here (EXT-CB forces estimate_ifb on, so rx DCB states
exist).  cb_kaula_prior is turned OFF instead — with no CB columns it folds nothing.
- network.sticky_pivot warns INERT (the anchored clock datum has no pivot).
- mw_wl.uwl_enable / ewl_enable stay armed but are inert under dual (GPS EWL is L2/L5).
lane_carry is already off, so this costs nothing; expect zero lane rows at run end.
FRESH LINEAGE ONLY: frequency_mode, the bias source and the clock-gauge realization are
all fingerprinted.  Own paths; never resume onto another arm's snapshot.
